Here's the function, in `email_validator.py`:

```python
import re

_EMAIL_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<local>[A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+"
    r"(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+)*)"
    r"@"
    r"(?P<domain>(?:[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?\.)+"
    r"[A-Za-z]{2,63})$"
)


def is_valid_email(address: str) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(address, str) or len(address) > 254:
        return False
    match = _EMAIL_RE.match(address)
    if not match:
        return False
    return len(match.group("local")) <= 64
```

It catches the usual bad shapes: no `@`, missing top-level part, dots at the edges, doubled dots, hyphens at the edges of a domain piece, and over-long parts.

Two things it turns down on purpose: quoted names like `"john doe"@example.com`, and raw IP domains like `user@[192.0.2.1]`.

The file has a self-check at the bottom. Running it: 22/22 cases passed.
